# DBX

> Per-tenant memory engine for AI products: one isolated store per customer, holding working state and vector memory.

- Site: https://dbxdb.co.in/
- Contact: hello@dbxdb.io
- License: Business Source License 1.1 (Apache 2.0 after four years)
- Source: https://github.com/vanshjain-0702/DBX-Database-Extreme
- Version: 1.3.0 (live vector migration, historical search, framework adapters, stronger isolation, encrypted replication, scoped support recovery). GHCR: ghcr.io/vanshjain-0702/dbx-orchestrator:v1.3.0. GitHub Release: https://github.com/vanshjain-0702/DBX-Database-Extreme/releases/tag/v1.3.0
- Announcement: https://dbxdb.co.in/posts.html#v1-3-0-2026-10-02
- Release notes and upgrade steps: https://github.com/vanshjain-0702/DBX-Database-Extreme/blob/v1.3.0/docs/releases/v1.3.0.md

## What it is

Self-hosted single binary. Orchestrator HTTP on :8000. Authenticated RESP on :6380.
Each tenant is a directory with its own WAL, HNSW (SQ8), and snapshots — not a key prefix on a shared cluster.

v1 supported profile: 100 tenants/node, 100k vectors/tenant, durable strings + vectors.
Async WAL replicas optional (primary acks locally). Raft, cluster, and non-string RESP mutations fail closed.

Operator HTTP (JWT on :8000): provision, keys, backup/restore, export/import,
hibernate/wake, GET /api/v1/tenants/{id}/usage, GET /api/usage.
Recall (RESP): VSEARCH, VSIM (neighbors of a stored id), VFUSE (late-fusion across named SPACE graphs).
Embeddings stay with the caller. DBX does not run a model.
Operational vector upgrades: VMIGRATE builds and promotes a non-empty shadow index while
the current index remains searchable; VSEARCH AS_OF <unix-nanoseconds> replays retained
vector WAL history into a temporary index for audit and incident reproduction. Migration
requires caller-side re-embedding, uses temporary storage, and is not yet a replicated WAL
protocol. AS_OF is slower than current search and bounded by WAL retention.
Dashboard Tenant keys: /cluster/{id}/keys (secret shown once).
Prometheus: GET /metrics (Bearer JWT or internal token in production). JSON: GET /t/{id}/metrics.

Density: CI soaks 12 idle / 4 active. Operators run `make soak` (100 idle / 25 active).
That is not a 100-orchestrator-process soak. 15-minute path: examples/quickstart.py.
LangChain example: examples/langchain-rag. Next.js SETEX: examples/nextjs-cache.
Python checks: `make python-check` (pytest skips live AUTH without env).

Public site source: website/.
Live: https://dbxdb.co.in/
Incubation pitch: https://dbxdb.co.in/pitch.html
Local preview: `make site`. Public host: dbxdb.co.in.
Docker: deploy/Dockerfile. GHCR ghcr.io/vanshjain-0702/dbx-orchestrator:v1.3.0 (and :latest on version tags or GitHub Releases). Image defaults to DBX_ISOLATION_MODE=strict; docker run requires DBX_KEK (64 hex) or -e DBX_ISOLATION_MODE=inprocess. Compose: cp .env.example .env (repo root, include KEK), then docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build (or make docker-up). Python: pip install -e sdk/python before `from dbx import DBXClient`. SDK version 1.3.0; LangChain and LlamaIndex optional extras are available.

Support extension 0.4.0 is included separately with DBX 1.3.0. It is manually
started and uses support-specific, tenant-allowlisted read and optional wake
capabilities. Wake requires a durable audit and is rate-limited; client post-checks
verify recovery. It cannot repair arbitrary bugs, restore/delete customer data,
or change security/configuration. Coverage: 31 casebook entries, 43 support tests,
and 1,340 synthetic diagnosis/recovery-policy drills; no model-weight training.
WAL replication uses mutual HMAC-SHA256 authentication and per-connection
AES-256-GCM frames. Strict Linux workers require CGO_ENABLED=0. Vector payload
rows remain mmap plaintext and need encrypted storage for at-rest confidentiality.

Launch: reader keys cannot SET/VADD/SETEX. Production /metrics needs Bearer. No default
superuser on orchestrator tenants. TLS on :8000. Not SOC 2. Not a cluster.

## Do not say

Redis replacement. All-in-one AI database. Cheaper than Pinecone. Scales to billions of vectors. SOC 2.

## Feature deep-dives

### Multi-tenant vector database isolation
DBX is a multi-tenant vector database that isolates each tenant into its own directory, write-ahead log (WAL), HNSW vector index, and snapshot lineage. Isolation is structural — not a key prefix. Each tenant is a sealed execution domain on Linux strict mode (process-level Landlock, per-tenant encryption keys). Provision, back up, restore, and delete target exactly one customer. Certified profile: 100 tenants/node, 100k vectors/tenant.
Page: https://dbxdb.co.in/features/per-tenant-isolation.html

### Zero-downtime vector migration (VMIGRATE)
VMIGRATE builds a shadow index on disk while the current index keeps serving reads. Stream caller-generated vectors with new dimensions or encodings, then promote the non-empty shadow with an atomic lifecycle swap. Cancel keeps the current index untouched. Empty migrations are rejected. Per-tenant, WAL-durable.
Page: https://dbxdb.co.in/features/shadow-migration.html

### Historical vector search / time-travel (VSEARCH AS_OF)
VSEARCH AS_OF replays retained vector WAL history into a temporary index to reconstruct embeddings at a specific unix nanosecond timestamp. Designed for RAG incident reproduction, compliance audit trails (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA), and embedding quality regression detection. Slower than current-state queries. Bounded by WAL retention.
Page: https://dbxdb.co.in/features/time-travel-vector-search.html

### Late fusion vector search (VFUSE)
VFUSE searches each named SPACE graph independently using cosine similarity, then computes a weighted sum of per-space scores. Combine text + image + code embeddings in one query without a multimodal model. Missing ids score 0. Not hybrid sparse+dense search.
Page: https://dbxdb.co.in/features/late-fusion-vector-search.html

### RESP-compatible KV + HNSW engine
DBX speaks RESP, so redis-py, ioredis, and go-redis connect without a custom driver. KV with TTL (session, scratchpad, rate counters) and HNSW vectors (semantic recall) live in one process, one connection, one backup. LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters available. Not a Redis replacement — non-string RESP mutation families fail closed.
Page: https://dbxdb.co.in/features/redis-compatible-memory.html

### SQ8 scalar quantization and mmap density
Vectors stored as 8-bit scalar-quantized (SQ8) rows in mmap'd files with asymmetric distance computation at query time. ~4x memory savings over float32. Idle tenants in page cache (~14-17 MiB RSS per idle worker). Cost scales with active tenants, not provisioned tenants. ANN p50: 2.304 ms.
Page: https://dbxdb.co.in/features/scalar-quantization-sq8.html
